sections.title: Which one? Both? Neither?
sections.content: To ask which of two things, join them with *vagy* (or): *Az almát vagy a körtét kéred?* The answer is one of them: *A körtét kérem.* To take both, put *is* after each thing: *Az almát is, a körtét is kérem.* To leave one, put *nem* before the verb: *A körtét nem kérem.* The article stays, so the verb stays definite.

sections.title: Choosing
rows: Az almát vagy a körtét kéred?
Do you take the apple or the pear?
Az almát is, a körtét is kérem.
I take both the apple and the pear.

items.spanish: Az almát vagy a körtét kéred?
items.english: Do you take the apple or the pear?

items.spanish: Az almát is, a körtét is kérem.
items.english: I'll take both the apple and the pear.

items.spanish: A paprikát vagy az uborkát veszik?
items.english: Are they taking the pepper or the cucumber?
We are buying the cucumber too.

sections.content: *Is* goes right after the word it belongs to, not at the end of the sentence: *Az almát is kérem*, as in *Banánokat is kérek*. Say *is* once after each thing for "both ... and".
